rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, al-sirat means a road or path.
rows.anchor: الصراط في اللغة : الطريق .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes give a literal road sense, illustrated by the road on which people are threatened and the path to Hell.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes also use al-sirat for religion, as in the request for the straight path and God's path to be followed.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirteenth Qur'anic sense listed for guidance is reform, illustrated by God's not guiding the treacherous plot.
rows.anchor: والثالث عشر : الإصلاح . ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourteenth sense is a messenger: the guidance sent to the Israelites and in Taha is glossed as a messenger.
rows.anchor: والرابع عشر : الرسول . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that the guidance in this instance means the Book.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : الهدى ها هنا الكتاب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifteenth sense is discernment, illustrated by the unbelievers who were not guided in their trade.
rows.anchor: والخامس عشر : الاستبصار . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The sixteenth sense is a guide or indicator; in Moses's request, it can mean someone to show him the way to the fire if it is not actually fire.
rows.anchor: والسادس عشر : الدليل . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventeenth sense is teaching, as in God's teaching people the practices of those before them.
rows.anchor: والسابع عشر : التعليم . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eighteenth sense is excellence or superiority: 'more guided' means better in way.
rows.anchor: والثامن عشر : الفضل . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nineteenth sense is leading or directing, as in driving people toward the path to Hell.
rows.anchor: والتاسع عشر : التقديم . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twentieth sense is dying while adhering to Islam, expressed by the one who repents, believes, acts righteously, then is guided.
rows.anchor: منه قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-first sense is reward, in the statement that guidance is incumbent upon God.
rows.anchor: والحادي والعشرون : الثواب . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-second sense is reminders: 'He found you astray and guided you' means He reminded you after forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: والثاني والعشرون : الأذكار . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في الضحى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-third sense is correctness, as in asking whether a person is on the right guidance.
rows.anchor: والثالث والعشرون : الصواب . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twenty-fourth sense is steadfastness: the prayer asks God to keep the worshippers on the straight path.
rows.anchor: الثبات . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically, ni'ma is what gives a person enjoyment in life.
rows.anchor: النعمة : ما يحصل للإنسان به التنعم في العيش .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun can mean a favor or gracious benefaction, and can also mean wealth; al-na'ama is a gentle wind.
rows.anchor: و النعمة : المنة ، ومثلها النعماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open initial n, ni'ma denotes luxurious living; a mutana'im is one living in luxury, and to favor one's children is to make them live luxuriously.
rows.anchor: فأما النعمة - بفتح النون - فهي التنعم . والمتنعم : المترف .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also distinguishes the verb نعم as 'yes' (opposed to لا), with a variant vowel, and as the opposite of بئس.
rows.anchor: وقد تكسر عينها ، ونعم ضد بئس .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is gracious favor, illustrated by the command to remember God's favor and its parallel in al-Ahzab.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A second sense is religion and Scripture, as in warnings against exchanging God's favor after it came.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third sense is Muhammad, whom people recognize as God's favor and then deny.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fourth sense is reward, as believers rejoice in a favor from God and bounty.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fifth sense is prophethood, applied to those favored in al-Fatiha and to the command to proclaim the Lord's favor.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A sixth sense is mercy, as in the phrase 'bounty from God and favor.'
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A seventh sense is beneficence, as in the statement that no one has a favor owed to be repaid.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: An eighth sense is ample livelihood, illustrated by God's abundant outward and inward blessings.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A ninth sense is Islam, in God's favor upon Zayd in the al-Ahzab passage.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A tenth sense is emancipation: God's favor to Zayd was Islam, while the Prophet's favor was freeing Zayd ibn Haritha.
rows.anchor: العتق . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الأحزاب ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nas denotes human beings; its singular is insan and its plurals include nas and anasi.
rows.anchor: الناس : [ اسم ] للحيوان الآدمي . وواحد الناس إنسان .

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris links the name al-ins to humans being visible or manifest.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : سمي الإنس إنسا لظهورهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related verb آنست can mean seeing a thing, hearing a sound, or knowing; anis is whatever provides company or solace.
rows.anchor: ويقال : آنست الشيء : رأيته . وآنست الصوت : سمعته .

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: With a doubled s, nas means thirsty; an anonymous rajaz line using نسا is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: والناس بتشديد السين : العطشان . قال الراجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca is called al-nasiya because water is scarce there.
rows.anchor: ويقال لمكة : الناسية ، لقلة الماء بها .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One Qur'anic referent of al-nas is Muhammad, in the verse about people envying what God gave him.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another referent is the other messengers, in the statement that believers are witnesses over the people.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative grammatical reading takes على in the witnesses verse in the sense of لام.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن ( على ) ( 131 / أ ) ها هنا بمعنى ' اللام '

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-nas can mean believers, as in the curse against those who disbelieve after having believed.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: It can mean believing people of the Torah, identified here as Ibn Salam and his companions.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In the scope verses, al-nas refers to the people of Mecca; the wording remains general although the address is directed to Meccans.
rows.anchor: وهو اللفظ عام وإن خوطب به أهل مكة .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A further referent is the Jews, in the statement about there being no argument for the people against the believers.
rows.anchor: والسادس : اليهود . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-nas can also refer to the Children of Israel, as in the Torah and Gospel being sent as guidance for people and Jesus's address about taking him and his mother as gods.
rows.anchor: والسابع : بنو إسرائيل . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says la'alla can mean 'so that'; Arabs use it to express purpose, and an anonymous couplet's la'alla-na illustrates that use.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني : أحدها : بمعنى ' كي ' .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous couplet says 'hold back from war so that we may hold back'; its poet is not named, and لعلنا witnesses the purpose sense.
rows.anchor: وقلتم لنا كفوا الحروب لعلنا … نكف ووثقتم لنا كل موثق …

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: A second Arabic sense is conjecture, as in 'I think I will make pilgrimage this year.'
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: A third Arabic sense is 'perhaps' or 'it may be,' as in the example that Abd Allah may rise.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: A fourth Arabic sense is interrogation, as in asking whether someone intends to insult the speaker and be punished.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In Qur'anic use, la'alla can express purpose: people worship their Lord so that they may become mindful of Him.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A Qur'anic sense is hope or expectation, expressed in Moses and Aaron's hope that Pharaoh may remember or fear and in the hope God may bring about a matter.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third Qur'anic sense is 'as if': the people build structures as though they expected to live forever.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In origin, al-birr names what brings benefit to the person receiving someone's kindness.
rows.anchor: البر في الأصل : اسم لما يحصل به للمبرور النفع

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris gives birr as the opposite of disobedience and as truth; the entry also notes obedience to one's Lord, superiority over one's peers, arak fruit, and excessive talk as related forms.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والبر : ضد العقوق . والبر : الصدق .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is maintaining kinship, in commands to be righteous toward relatives and just toward non-hostile people.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is obedience, illustrated by cooperation in righteousness, dutifulness to parents, righteous conversation, and the record and character of the righteous angels.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third Qur'anic sense is piety, including the rebuke for commanding others to be righteous while neglecting oneself and the description of true righteousness.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that in the verse about giving from what one loves, attaining birr means attaining Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لن تنالوا الجنة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A masjid is a place of prostration; conventionally it is an Islamic building for prayer, analogous to a church for Jews and a sales (church) for Christians.
rows.anchor: المسجد : اسم لموضع السجود . وجمعه : مساجد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic referent is the Jerusalem sanctuary, in the verse about preventing God's name from being mentioned in His mosques.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن المسجد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second referent is the Sacred Mosque, cited in two verses about the polytheists not maintaining God's mosques and about the Sacred Mosque itself.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن المسجد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third referent is the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, while another view identifies the cited mosque as Quba.
rows.anchor: والثالث : مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification of the mosque founded on piety is the mosque of Quba.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مسجد قباء .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fourth referent is the Mosque of Dhirar, the mosque built to cause harm and disbelief.
rows.anchor: والرابع : مسجد الضرار . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fifth referent is Mecca and its sanctuary, in passages about the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people or barring access to it.
rows.anchor: والخامس : مكة والحرم . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A sixth sense is all mosques, in the verse listing monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques that would otherwise be demolished.
rows.anchor: والسادس : [ جميع ] المساجد . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A seventh sense is the human limbs on which one prostrates, applied to the mosques belonging to God; some exegetes group this with the preceding all-mosques sense.
rows.anchor: والسابع : أعضاء الإنسان التي يسجد عليها . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the linguistic root of foolishness is lightness of judgment; a thin, worn garment can also be called safih.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : ( 69 / ب ) أصل السفه في اللغة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris uses the verb for wind bending trees; Dhu al-Rumma's poem uses تسفهت to describe the wind's effect on the tops of trees.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : يقال تسفهت الريح [ الشجر ]

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line is evidence for تسفهت meaning that the breeze swayed the tree tops.
rows.anchor: فمادت كما مادت رماح تسفهت … أعاليها مر الرياح النواسم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One Qur'anic sense is ignorant people, as in the taunt asking whether the believers should believe like fools.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السفهاء في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The people called fools in this qibla verse are identified as Jews; another view says they are hypocrites.
rows.anchor: والثاني : اليهود . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification of the fools who question the change of qibla is the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم المنافقون .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In the verse about property guardianship, al-sufaha' refers to women and children.
rows.anchor: والثالث : النساء والصبيان . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fourth sense is ruin: the one who turns away from Abraham's religion has ruined himself.
rows.anchor: والرابع : السفه الهلاك . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fi can mean 'at' in the cited examples about being weak among a people, once favored among them, and living among them for years.
rows.anchor: والسادس : بمعنى عند . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi can stand in the sense of bi in the examples of God's coming amid clouds and someone being apart.
rows.anchor: والسابع : بمعنى ' الباء ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the qibla passage, fi means 'toward' the sky, describing the Prophet's repeated turning of his face in that direction.
rows.anchor: والثامن : بمعنى نحو . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في البقرة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi can mean 'about' or 'concerning,' as in disputing over names invented by people and their fathers.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : بمعنى ' عن ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi can mean 'for,' as in striving for God with due striving and those who strive for Him.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : بمعنى ' اللام ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth sense of du'a is asking or supplication, as in God's answering the caller, Moses being asked to pray for relief, and the condemned asking Hell's keepers to pray for them.
rows.anchor: والخامس : السؤال . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth sense is questioning: asking Moses to clarify what the cow is, or asking the false gods whether they are deities.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الاستفهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventh sense is punishment: the fire calls and torments those who turned away.
rows.anchor: والسابع : العذاب . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurb ordinarily means nearness in distance, the opposite of remoteness; qurban can be an offering to God or a king's close associates.
rows.anchor: الأصل في القرب : أنه الدنو من المسافة . وضده : البعد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb 'aqrabat is used of a sheep nearing delivery, but not of a she-camel.
rows.anchor: واقربت الشاة دنا نتاجها . لا يقال : للناقة : اقربت .

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit describes a garment as muqarib and says this label is not used when it is not good.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : ثوب مقارب ، ولا يقال مقارب إذا لم يكن جيدا .

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another linguist says a garment called muqarib with kasra is poor, while with fatha it is inexpensive.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : ثوب مقارب - بكسر الراء - ليس بجيد - وبفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qarib is a small boat traveling with larger sea ships for quick errands; the word also means a person seeking water at night.
rows.anchor: والقارب : سفينة صغيرة تكون مع أصحاب السفن البحرية

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris transmits that some linguists restrict qarib, the water-seeker, to someone who seeks water at night rather than by day.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن فارس عن بعض اللغويين : أنه لا يقال ذلك لطالب الماء نهارا .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is intercourse, in the prohibition against approaching wives during menstruation.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القرب في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is answering: God's 'I am near' means that He responds, as does 'He is all-hearing, near.'
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القرب في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third sense is nearness in time, in the soon-coming punishment and in the approaching Reckoning and true promise.
rows.anchor: والثالث : قرب الزمان . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fourth sense is what is more correct, as in the seeker hoping to find a path closer to right guidance.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الأصوب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fifth sense is gentleness or affection, describing the Christians as closest in affection to the believers.
rows.anchor: والخامس : اللين . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The sixth sense is kinship, in the passages about affection for close relatives and feeding a poor person who is near of kin.
rows.anchor: والسادس : القرابة . ومنه قوله تعالى في عسق

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The seventh sense is a time just before the angel of death is seen, as in those who repent shortly before death.
rows.anchor: والسابع : ما قبل معاينة الملك . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The eighth sense is eating, as in the prohibition against Adam and Eve approaching the tree.
rows.anchor: والثامن : الأكل . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The ninth sense is entering prayer, as in the prohibition against approaching prayer while intoxicated.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : الدخول في الصلاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One listed sense is refusal, illustrated by people who turn away from migration or from the revealed judgment.
rows.anchor: في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sense is turning away, as in several commands and descriptions of people who refuse the Prophet's message.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الإعراض ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth sense is fleeing in battle, illustrated by commands against turning one's back and reports of defeated forces.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الهزيمة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنفال

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Some add a fifth sense, authority or becoming a ruler; al-Dahhak and Mujahid gloss the verse as becoming a governor over the land.
rows.anchor: وهو الولاية ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj are also reported to interpret the verse's tawalla as becoming angry.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس ، وابن جريج ، أن معنى تولى : غضب .

rows.speaker: مقاتل وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Some, including Muqatil and Ibn Qutayba, place this usage under the separate sense of departing or turning away.
rows.anchor: منهم : مقاتل ، وابن قتيبة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasad is the verbal noun of becoming corrupt; it means a change from soundness and may describe an object while it remains, when it is undone, or when it vanishes.
rows.anchor: والفساد : تغير عما كان عليه من الصلاح . وقد يقال في الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption can occur in religion through disobedience or disbelief; the entry also distinguishes invalid worship, contracts, testimony, claims, speech, and actions by their legal or practical defects.
rows.anchor: الفساد في الدين كما يذكر في الذات . فتارة يكون بالعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some invalid rites, such as Hajj and Umrah, must still be completed, whereas an invalid prayer is not continued; contracts are corrupt when legal conditions are unmet.
rows.anchor: ومن العبادات ما يلزم المضي في فاسدها ، كالحج والعمرة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry calls testimony corrupt when it should not ground a judgment, a claim corrupt when it is not heard, speech corrupt when disordered, and acts corrupt when they are not credited.
rows.anchor: وفي الشهادة ، إذا لم يجب الحكم بها . وفي الدعاوي إذا لم تسمع

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is disobedience, as in the hypocrites' prohibition against spreading corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفساد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is destruction: if there were gods besides God in the heavens and earth, both would be ruined.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفساد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is drought and diminished vegetation, as in the appearance of corruption on land and sea.
rows.anchor: والثالث : قحط المطر ( وقلة النبات ) . ومنه قوله تعالى في الروم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth sense is killing: Pharaoh feared Moses and his people would kill Egypt's people; Gog and Magog are called corrupt because they kill people, as is Pharaoh's feared outcome in Ghafir.
rows.anchor: والرابع : القتل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fifth sense is ruin, applied to the land-corrupting plot in this verse and to conquerors who ruin a town.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الخراب . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The sixth sense is disbelief, in the call for people of understanding to forbid corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الكفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The seventh sense is sorcery, as in Moses's statement that God does not make the work of sorcerers succeed.
rows.anchor: والسابع : السحر . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah defines harth as land made workable for planting; it also names the first track of a horse and the length reached by seed or furrow.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله رحمه الله الحرث اسم لكل ما ذللته

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says harth means gathering; Harith is named from it, and the saying about cultivating for worldly life means working for it as if one would live forever.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الحرث : الجمع . وبه سمي الرجل حارثا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also uses harth for a wife as the man's planting ground for children and says to 'cultivate the Qur'an' means to recite it often.
rows.anchor: والمرأة : حرث الرجل . لأنها مزدرع ولده ويقولون أحرث القرآن

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is reward, as in the one who seeks the harvest of the Hereafter receiving more of it.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحرث في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is cultivated land, in verses about cattle churning the soil and the destruction of crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحرث في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is the place where children are conceived, in the address comparing wives to a field.
rows.anchor: منبت الولد ، ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halak and fasad are close in meaning: corruption occurs while the object remains, whereas destruction can occur whether it remains or is gone; the terms overlap in death, annihilation, invalidated proof, and disabled benefits.
rows.anchor: الهلاك والفساد يتقاربان . إلا أن الفساد يكون مع بقاء العين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense of halak is death, including the death of people in a town and the declaration that all things perish save God's face.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الهلاك في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is punishment, in passages about punished towns and peoples, including the generations with finer possessions and appearance.
rows.anchor: والثاني : العذاب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجر

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is misguidance or loss: 'my authority perished from me' means that my proof was lost.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الضلال . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth sense is corruption, as in destroying crops and offspring or wasting a great amount of wealth.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الفساد . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the continuation on yawm, one sense is Judgment Day, the day when no soul is wronged and the Day of Decision is appointed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ﴾ ، وفي النبأ :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second listed sense of yawm is the day of Arafah, identified with the day God's religion was perfected.
rows.anchor: والثالث : يوم عرفة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further sense of yawm is a general occasion or time, as in giving the due of a crop at harvest.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الحين . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can also mean a measure of time: Gabriel's descent and ascent take a period that would require a thousand years for another to ascend.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الوقت . ومنه قوله تعالى في سجدة لقمان

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the root sense of 'izza is strength; 'azza 'alayya means that an affair became hard on me.
rows.anchor: ذكر أبو سليمان الدمشقي : ان أصل العزة : الشدة .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is greatness or might, as in swearing by Pharaoh's might or by God's might.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن العزة في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is invulnerability or power, in the statement that all might belongs to God.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن العزة في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third sense is haughty zeal: when told to fear God, the wrongdoer is seized by pride that draws him to sin; the disbelievers also persist in arrogance and opposition.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الحمية . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ba'l can mean husband, companion, or lord; it can also refer to land watered by its own roots without rain.
rows.anchor: البعل يقال ويراد به : الزوج ، والصاحب ، والرب .

rows.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah says a husband is called a woman's ba'l because she is like the field in which a child grows, and the man's fluid is its irrigation.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : وسمي الزوج بعلا للمرأة لأنها كأرض الحرث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account derives ba'l from elevation: a husband is ba'l because he is above the woman.
rows.anchor: وقيل البعل : العلو في الأصل . والزوج بعل : لعلوه على المرأة .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is husband, in the divorce verse and in Shu'ayb's wife calling him her husband.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البعل في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is the idol Ba'l, whom the people are asked whether they worship while abandoning the best of creators.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البعل في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijal is the plural of rajul and ordinarily names human males after puberty; some derive it from strength, and the entry notes related senses including strong walkers, spontaneous speech, combed hair, a walker, and a locust segment.
rows.anchor: الرجال جمع : رجل ، فهو اسم لذكور بني آدم بعد البلوغ .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qur'anic referent is messengers, as in the statement that only men were sent before Muhammad and received revelation.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A second referent is angels, in the men on the heights who recognize people by their marks.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third referent is the Prophet's steadfast Companions in battle, who remained true to their covenant with God.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fourth referent is the people of Quba, praised for loving purification.
rows.anchor: والرابع : أهل قباء . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A fifth referent is men who keep the appointed prayer times and are not distracted by trade.
rows.anchor: والخامس : المحافظون على أوقات الصلاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The sixth referent is oppressed believing men among the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والسادس : المقهورون من مؤمني أهل مكة .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The seventh referent is poor Muslims, whom the people of Hell say they once counted among the wicked.
rows.anchor: والسابع : فقراء المسلمين . ومنه قوله تعالى في صاد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The eighth sense is people walking on foot, in the permission to pray on foot or mounted and the pilgrimage command to come walking.
rows.anchor: والثامن : المشاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The ninth sense is husbands, as in the statement that men have a degree over women and are responsible for them.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : الأزواج . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The tenth sense is males, in the statements that God spread many men and that Muhammad is not the father of any of the community's men.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : الذكور . ومنه قوله تعالى في النساء
